chunks: Al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from his father 'Ali ibn Yaqtin:
he said: I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about al-madhy — does it break wudu? He said: 'If it is from [sexual] desire, it breaks [it].'

key_terms.اَلْمَذْيِ: al-madhy: thin pre-seminal fluid emitted during sexual arousal, distinct from semen (manī) and thicker fluid (wadhy)
key_terms.اَلْوُضُوءَ: wudu: ritual ablution required before salat; its nullification necessitates renewal before prayer
key_terms.شَهْوَةٍ: shahwa: sexual desire or arousal; the operative condition in the Imam's legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Does al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) break wudu according to Shia hadith from Imam al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: This hadith records a jurisprudential question posed by 'Ali ibn Yaqtin — a trusted companion and minister of Imam al-Kadhim (AS) — on whether the emission of al-madhy (pre-seminal fluid) invalidates ritual ablution. The Imam's ruling is conditional: al-madhy nullifies wudu only when it results from sexual desire or arousal, implying that inadvertent or non-arousal emission does not carry the same consequence.
